bogonResponse.why: A bogon is answered locally in the full max shape. Every flag is present and false, every detail object is present and empty, and is_bogon marks it as computed rather than served.

lookup.name: free-not-vpn
lookup.why: The free shape. Every tier-gated member is absent, which means not-in-your-plan and must not read as false.

lookup.name: starter-vpn-hit
lookup.why: Starter buys the vpn object and the four classification FLAGS, but none of their detail objects.

lookup.name: scale-empty-object-means-flag-false
lookup.why: An empty detail object beside a false flag means not-found. It must not be confused with an absent member.

lookup.name: max-full-shape
lookup.why: Max adds confidence and method on vpn, plus the three proxy families.

lookup.name: unattributed-range-keeps-empty-provider
lookup.why: A populated object always carries every key. An unattributed range has an empty provider string, never a missing one.

lookup.name: max-nothing-found
lookup.why: A served all-negative Max answer. This is the only case that pins EVERY tier-gated flag as present-and-false, so a per-field slip that maps on truthiness rather than presence cannot hide behind the members other cases happen to set true.

body.error: source address not allowed for this API key

errors.name: not-found-is-not-retryable
errors.why: A 404 is a CLIENT error. Falling through to the server_error default makes it retryable, so a bad dataset id is retried before it fails. Only 5xx and transport failures are retryable.

errors.name: rate-limited-is-retryable
errors.why: Retry-After present. This is the API protecting itself and retrying WILL succeed.

errors.name: keyless-daily-quota-is-not-retryable
errors.why: No Retry-After. The keyless daily allowance is spent and retrying will not help.

body.error: daily limit for unauthenticated requests exceeded; use an API key
request allowance exceeded; raise or remove your overage limit

batch.name: dedup-bogon-and-order-free-keying
batch.why: Duplicates collapse to one entry, bogons never reach the network, and what is left goes to POST /batch in ONE request rather than one request per address. The result is keyed by IP so input order stops mattering.

batch.name: partial-failure-does-not-fail-the-batch
batch.why: One address erroring must leave the others answered; the failure is carried in that key's value. The server reports it per entry as {status, error}, and the entry is classified by that status exactly as a single lookup answering it would be.

batch.name: cache-hit-issues-no-second-request
batch.why: The second batch over the same address is served entirely from the per-client cache.

batch.name: chunks-of-one-thousand
batch.why: POST /batch takes at most 1000 addresses per call, so a larger input is sent in chunks of 1000 and every address is still answered exactly once.

batch.name: an-entry-error-is-classified-by-its-status
batch.why: A per-entry failure arrives as {status, error} with no headers, so a 429 there is always a spent allowance (never a throttle, which refuses the whole call with Retry-After) and a 500 is a server error. Neither is retried per entry; the whole call's retry rule is unchanged.

middleware.why: The framework middleware contract: how a block condition is evaluated, and which conditions must be refused outright. Field names are the WIRE names; each SDK maps them to its own idiom exactly as it maps a response.

conditions.name: flag-true-matches
conditions.why: The simplest condition there is: a served flag that is true.

conditions.name: flag-true-against-false
conditions.why: A served flag that is false does not match.

conditions.name: flag-absent-is-not-false
conditions.why: The member is not in this plan, so the term can never match and must be reported. Absent means not-in-your-plan, never checked-and-no.

conditions.name: nested-provider-exact
conditions.why: A condition reaches the evidence fields, not just the flags.

conditions.name: nested-provider-case-insensitive
conditions.why: Providers are lowercase slugs on the wire; a caller should not have to know that.

conditions.name: nested-provider-mismatch
conditions.why: A different provider does not match.

conditions.name: and-across-members
conditions.why: Every member named must hold.

conditions.name: and-one-fails
conditions.why: One failing term fails the whole condition.

conditions.name: or-list-second-matches
conditions.why: A list is OR: any one entry blocking is enough.

conditions.name: or-list-none-match
conditions.why: A list where nothing matches does not block.

conditions.name: array-any-of
conditions.why: An array value is any-of, for an enum-like field.

conditions.name: array-none-of
conditions.why: An any-of that contains nothing the answer carries.

conditions.name: numeric-gte-inside
conditions.why: The evidence counters are only useful with a threshold.

conditions.name: numeric-gte-outside
conditions.why: Below the threshold does not match.

conditions.name: numeric-range-inside
conditions.why: Every bound present must hold, so two of them are a range.

conditions.name: numeric-exclusive-bound
conditions.why: gt and lt are strict. Pinned because an off-by-one here reads as a working filter.

conditions.name: numeric-inclusive-lower-bound
conditions.why: gte INCLUDES the bound. hits is exactly 7 here, so a gte that compares strictly still passes every other numeric case and fails only this one.

conditions.name: numeric-inclusive-upper-bound
conditions.why: lte INCLUDES the bound, the mirror of the case above.

conditions.name: numeric-exclusive-upper-bound
conditions.why: lt EXCLUDES it. Together with numeric-exclusive-bound this pins all four comparators at the one value where inclusive and strict disagree.

conditions.name: fractional-bound-on-an-integer-member
conditions.why: Every numeric member the API serves is an integer, so the FRACTION has to come from the bound. Pinned because a comparison done in integers would round the bound and quietly widen or narrow the rule.

conditions.name: numeric-bound-on-absent-member
conditions.why: A bound against a member this plan does not serve matches nothing and is reported.

conditions.name: false-entry-is-ignored
conditions.why: A false entry states nothing, so the remaining term decides. There is deliberately no way to write block-when-false, which would read as blocking everybody.

conditions.name: null-entry-is-ignored
conditions.why: Null is ignored for the same reason false is.

conditions.name: empty-detail-is-a-real-false
conditions.why: An empty detail object means the flag above it is false. That is a served answer, not a plan gap, so it must not be reported as missing.

conditions.name: bogon-is-exempt
conditions.why: A locally answered bogon carries every member by construction, so reporting coverage from it would tell a free-tier caller they hold the full plan.

invalidConditions.name: empty-condition
invalidConditions.why: Nothing to satisfy means it matches every answer, which is a total outage.

invalidConditions.name: every-entry-ignored
invalidConditions.why: Ignoring false leaves this constraining nothing, so it must be refused rather than silently blocking everybody.

invalidConditions.name: empty-nested-object
invalidConditions.why: An empty nested object asserts only that the member is in your plan.
